description: The worlds an eval case's project can be set in. A world is a programming language and a business domain, with a small project that builds it, so the cases do not all sit in the one world their author knew. A live case, which builds a project with its own fixture.sh, names its world as a `world:<name>` tag beside its `claim:`, `tier:`, and `shape:` tags. A routing, roles, or trigger case builds no project, so it names none. The schema is schemas/eval-worlds.schema.json, and src/aidd/evals/worlds.py reads this file. The languages are in alphabetical order with `none` last, and the worlds follow the languages, then the domains, each in alphabetical order: add one where that order places it. A world's name is its language and its domain. `cap` is the most of the live cases any one world, language, or domain may have. The cap holds for every world, language, and domain, `none` and `general` too. `over_cap` lists what has more than `cap` today, with its case count, and a count may only fall: move cases to another world to lower it.
